- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is low, raise forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% above recent mean), apply a 10–15 day lag correction to prevent overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true mean by > 2.5% over 30d, apply downward bias adjustment proportional to sentiment volatility.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., +1.0 → -0.67 → +1.0), reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to account for mean reversion.  
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward trend, assume mean reversion and adjust forecast toward 30d moving average.
